tool.name: Cutadapt Demultiplex
tool.description: paired-end reads using combinatorial MID barcodes
tool.command:
mkdir -p outputs &&
## Sort every read pair into a file pair named after the barcode combination it ## carries. Barcodes are searched at the 5' end of both mates, so a pair ends up ## in 'temp_<forward barcode>-<reverse barcode>_R{1,2}.fastq'. Read pairs whose ## barcode is not recognised land in an 'unknown' file that is never collected. cutadapt -g 'file:$mids_file' -G 'file:$mids_file' --error-rate '$error_rate' --no-indels --action=trim --cores \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} -o 'temp_{name1}-{name2}_R1.fastq' -p 'temp_{name1}-{name2}_R2.fastq' '$input_r1' '$input_r2' &&
## Keep only the barcode combinations listed in the table and rename them after ## their sample, so that Galaxy can discover them as a paired collection. python '$__tool_directory__/cutadapt_demultiplex.py' '$combinations_file' --prefix 'temp_' --outdir 'outputs'

param.name: mids_file
param.label: MID sequences
param.help: FASTA file with one entry per MID. The sequence names are used as the barcode names in the combinations table below.

param.name: combinations_file
param.label: Allowed MID combinations
param.help: Tabular file with three columns: sample name, forward MID name, reverse MID name. A header line starting with 'Sample' is ignored.

param.label: Maximum error rate
param.help: Fraction of the MID sequence that is allowed to mismatch. The default of 0.1 allows one mismatch per ten barcode bases, 0 requires an exact match.

has_text.text: no read pair carried this combination

tool.help:
**What it does**
Demultiplexes paired-end reads that were multiplexed with a MID (Multiplex IDentifier) barcode on *both* the forward and the reverse read, and returns one element per sample in a paired collection.
Cutadapt is run in `combinatorial demultiplexing`_ mode: every read pair is sorted by the pair of barcodes it carries, and the barcodes are trimmed off. A table of the sample/barcode combinations that were actually multiplexed is then used to keep the expected combinations and to name them after their sample. Read pairs carrying any other combination, including pairs in which a barcode was not recognised at all, are discarded.
That last step is what distinguishes this tool from the demultiplexing mode of the regular **Cutadapt** tool, which demultiplexes single-end reads only. With *n* forward and *m* reverse barcodes, combinatorial demultiplexing produces up to *n* x *m* output files, and all but a handful of them are index hopping or sequencing noise rather than real samples.
-----
**Inputs**
*MID sequences* is a FASTA file with one entry per barcode. The names are what the combinations table refers to::
>MID13 ^NNACGTGCAGCG >MID70 ^NNNNNNNNTGAGTCAGTA
The full `Cutadapt adapter syntax`_ is available here. In the example above ``^`` anchors the barcode to the start of the read, and the leading ``N`` positions match the random unique molecular identifier in front of it. Anchoring the barcodes is strongly recommended, because an unanchored barcode can be matched anywhere inside a read.
*Allowed MID combinations* is a tabular file with three columns: the sample name, the barcode on the forward read and the barcode on the reverse read. A header line starting with ``Sample`` is optional and lines starting with ``#`` are ignored::
Sample MID1 MID2 patient_A MID13 MID70 patient_B MID13 MID16
Sample names become collection element identifiers, so they are restricted to letters, digits, ``.``, ``_``, ``+`` and ``-``, and each one has to be unique.
-----
**Output**
A paired collection with one element per sample that was found in the reads. The forward and reverse reads of each sample have their barcode trimmed off, which also removes any random prefix in front of the barcode.
Samples whose barcode combination occurs in none of the read pairs are skipped and listed in the job log instead of being added as empty datasets. If none of the expected combinations is found the job fails, because that almost always means the barcode names in the table do not match those in the FASTA file, or that the error rate is too strict.
.. _`combinatorial demultiplexing`: https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#combinatorial-demultiplexing .. _`Cutadapt adapter syntax`: https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#specifying-adapter-sequences
